ko.text: Quality at least 25 – or the satellite fails in orbit

name: Student Satellite
tagline: A small satellite and a launch window that won't wait
scope: A small research satellite: structure, electronics, solar panels, onboard software, ground station and vacuum chamber tests. The rocket launch is booked for a specific day.
intro: You lead a student team building a small research satellite. A seat on the rocket is booked – miss the launch and you fly a year later, which the grant wouldn't survive.
predWorld: Structure, electronics, long-lead component purchasing, vibration and vacuum tests, launch certification.
agileWorld: Onboard software, ground station and data processing. Tuned iteratively against a simulator, then against the real hardware.

terms.poGood: scientist who will use the data

dependency.hint: Software test on flight hardware waits for a predictive milestone – hardware delivery.

workstreams.name: Satellite mechanical structure
workstreams.why: Size and mass are set by the rocket; drawings get approved and it's built once.

workstreams.name: Flight component purchasing
workstreams.why: Space-certified parts have months-long lead times and fixed specs.

workstreams.name: Vibration and vacuum tests
workstreams.why: Test facilities are booked in advance and the rocket operator prescribes the test procedure.

workstreams.name: Power management firmware
workstreams.why: Careful: it's software, but safety-critical. It's specified upfront, tested with the hardware and frozen – no last-minute iterations.

workstreams.name: Onboard software for science measurements
workstreams.why: What the scientists need gets refined along the way; developed iteratively against a simulator.

workstreams.name: Ground station and data reception
workstreams.why: The software can be built piece by piece and improved even after launch.

workstreams.name: Data processing and visualization
workstreams.why: How to process the data only becomes clear from the first images – typical iterative work.

workstreams.name: Education program for schools
workstreams.why: Content is tuned to teacher and student feedback, version by version.

milestones.name: Flight hardware
milestones.okText: Flight hardware is delivered. From sprint 3 the software can be tested on the real board.
milestones.lateText: Hardware delivery slipped. Tests on the flight board can't start until sprint 4.

milestones.name: Vacuum chamber
milestones.okText: The vacuum chamber integration test passed: software and hardware work together.
milestones.lateText: The vacuum chamber integration test failed.

milestones.name: Vibration test
milestones.okText: The satellite passed the vibration test.
milestones.lateText: The vibration test slipped and has to be repeated.

milestones.name: Rocket launch
milestones.failText: The satellite wasn't ready for launch. The rocket left without it – the project failed.
milestones.okText: The satellite is on the rocket and lifting off! The first signal is coming in from orbit.

shift.title: The launch moves up
shift.text: The rocket's main payload is ready early – the launch moves two weeks forward. There's less time left than the team planned, and it can't be moved. Revealed factor: an immovable time window.
shift.lesson: When time shrinks and the deadline is absolute, freeze the configuration, let any further change through formal change control only – and cut scope deliberately. Otherwise last-minute tweaks break what was already verified.

gate.title: Critical Design Review (CDR)
gate.text: Agency experts assess whether the satellite design is mature enough to build the flight model. What will you present?
gate.lesson: A design review in a hybrid project judges hardware by documentation and tests, and software by what actually works on the simulator.

choices.text: Hardware documentation, test results and a live software demo on the simulator
choices.feedback: The review passed. The experts appreciated that you don't show software just on slides.

choices.text: Documentation only – we'll show the software once it's done
choices.feedback: The review passed with a caveat: "Software is a big risk." You got an extra audit.

choices.text: Ask to postpone the review
choices.feedback: Postponing the review pushes back the flight model build. The launch won't wait, though.

events.title: When to freeze the software?
events.text: Before integration you must decide when to "freeze" the onboard software. After the freeze, changes go only through formal change control.
events.lesson: For systems that are hard to fix after launch, freeze the core in time and design the rest to be updatable. Tweaking until the last minute is a gamble.

choices.text: Freeze the core (attitude, comms, safe mode), keep developing the rest with remote updates
choices.feedback: The core is stable and tested. Science features can be tuned even after launch.

choices.text: Freeze nothing and keep tweaking until the last minute
choices.feedback: The team has freedom – for now.

choices.text: Freeze absolutely everything right now
choices.feedback: Stable, but the scientists are disappointed: half of their requests didn't make it.

events.title: Batteries delayed
events.text: The certified battery supplier reports a three-week delay.
events.lesson: In space projects, backup suppliers and response plans are prepared in advance. Certification shortcuts don't pay off.

choices.text: Call in the backup certified supplier from the risk register
choices.feedback: The backup supplier was vetted. The batteries arrived only a week late.

choices.text: Wait and shorten the thermal tests
choices.feedback: The schedule holds; the tests are shorter.

choices.text: Buy cheaper uncertified batteries
choices.feedback: The batteries arrived right away. Their paperwork didn't.

events.title: Scientists want a different camera
events.text: After the demo the scientists declare the mission pointless without a better camera. But the camera is hardware and the design is almost done.
events.lesson: A change touching hardware goes through change control with an impact analysis. Part of the need can often be met with software.

choices.text: Analyze the impact via change control and offer software image enhancement
choices.feedback: The analysis showed a new camera would exceed the mass limit. Software sharpening satisfied the scientists.

choices.text: Give in – swap the camera
choices.feedback: The scientists are thrilled. The engineers, less so.

choices.text: Refuse without discussion
choices.feedback: The design is protected, but the scientists are losing the will to cooperate.

events.title: Lead programmer is leaving
events.text: The student who wrote the communication protocol is leaving for a semester abroad.
events.lesson: In temporary teams, knowledge sharing is insurance. Without it, the project depends on a single person.

choices.text: Pair programming and documentation now, remote collaboration later
choices.feedback: The sprint is slower, but three people now understand the protocol.

choices.text: Let it be, it'll work out somehow
choices.feedback: The student left. The code stayed.

choices.text: Pay them to leave only after the launch
choices.feedback: They stayed, but the knowledge is still in just one head.

events.title: Loose screw
events.text: During a preliminary vibration test, a screw on the antenna mount came loose.
events.lesson: With hardware defects, look for the cause in the procedure, not just that one screw. Otherwise the defect pops up elsewhere.

choices.text: Investigate the assembly procedure and check all similar joints
choices.feedback: Two more under-tightened screws turned up. The assembly procedure is fixed.

choices.text: Tighten that one screw and move on
choices.feedback: The screw is tight. Nobody checked the others.

choices.text: Repeat the whole vibration test
choices.feedback: The test passed, but nobody looked for the cause.

events.title: Report for the grant agency
events.text: The grant agency wants a progress report with a detailed Gantt – software included.
events.lesson: Hybrid reporting "translates": Gantt and milestones for hardware, delivered increments and a forecast for software.

choices.text: Gantt and milestones for hardware + an overview of delivered software increments
choices.feedback: The agency got an overview it understands, and the team doesn't have to plan every feature.

choices.text: A detailed Gantt for every software feature
choices.feedback: The plan is outdated after the first sprint.

choices.text: Send just a written narrative
choices.feedback: The agency asked for more details.

freeze_chaos.title: Last change broke the comms
freeze_chaos.text: A week before integration, a final "tiny tweak" to the software broke communication with Earth.
freeze_chaos.lesson: Without a frozen configuration, any change can break a verified whole. The safe move is to roll back to the last tested version.
freeze_chaos.unresolvedText: A bug from the last unfrozen change showed up in orbit.

choices.text: Roll back to the last tested version and add the change via change control
choices.feedback: Comms work again. The new feature will wait.

choices.text: Keep fixing on the fly until integration
choices.feedback: The fix broke two more things.

choices.text: Postpone the integration test
choices.feedback: There's time for a fix, but the launch didn't get any further away.

prehrivani.title: Electronics overheating
prehrivani.text: The shortened thermal test missed a problem: in vacuum, the board overheats.
prehrivani.lesson: Shortened tests only seem to save time. The defect is found later – at a higher price.
prehrivani.unresolvedText: The satellite overheats in orbit and must run in a limited mode.

choices.text: Add a heat sink and redo the full thermal test
choices.feedback: Problem solved, and the test was complete this time.

choices.text: Throttle performance in software and hope
choices.feedback: The scientists lose half their measurements.

choices.text: Swap the board for a different type
choices.feedback: Expensive, but it works.

certifikace.title: Certification rejected the batteries
certifikace.text: The rocket operator rejected the uncertified batteries. Without replacements, the satellite won't fly.
certifikace.lesson: Skimping on certification comes back with interest. The rocket operator's rules are not up for negotiation.
certifikace.unresolvedText: The uncertified batteries surfaced only at the final inspection.

choices.text: Order certified ones immediately with express delivery
choices.feedback: Painful, but the satellite will fly.

choices.text: Tweak the paperwork so it passes
choices.feedback: The fraud came out. The agency is considering clawing back the grant.

choices.text: Request an exemption
choices.feedback: An exemption takes weeks and may not go through.

hmotnost.title: The satellite is too heavy
hmotnost.text: The new camera is 200 grams heavier. The satellite exceeds the rocket's mass limit.
hmotnost.lesson: A hardware change without impact analysis has knock-on effects. That's why it goes through change control.
hmotnost.unresolvedText: The excess mass was solved at the last minute by stripping equipment.

choices.text: Go back to the original camera and explain it to the scientists
choices.feedback: It hurts, but the satellite will fly.

choices.text: Remove the backup battery
choices.feedback: The mass fits, but the satellite now has no energy reserve.

choices.text: Pay for a bigger slot on the rocket
choices.feedback: The grant can carry it – barely.

protokol.title: Nobody understands the protocol
protokol.text: There's a bug in the communication protocol, and the only person who understands it is abroad and not responding.
protokol.lesson: A knowledge island shows up exactly when time is shortest. Sharing knowledge is cheaper upfront.
protokol.unresolvedText: A bug in the protocol nobody understood limited data reception.

choices.text: Two people study and document the protocol, even if it slows the sprint
choices.feedback: Bug found, and more people now understand the protocol.

choices.text: Rewrite the protocol from scratch
choices.feedback: The new protocol has new bugs.

choices.text: Hire an outside expert
choices.feedback: The expert found the bug. The knowledge left with them.

antena.title: The antenna didn't deploy
antena.text: During the final test the deployable antenna didn't open – a different screw came loose in exactly the same way.
antena.lesson: Fixing the symptom instead of the cause just postpones the problem. The same defect shows up elsewhere.
antena.unresolvedText: After launch the antenna only opened halfway.

choices.text: Now investigate the whole assembly procedure and fix all joints
choices.feedback: The procedure is fixed. Late, but better than never.

choices.text: Tighten this screw too
choices.feedback: How many more screws are waiting?

choices.text: Replace the antenna with a fixed one
choices.feedback: More reliable, but with a weaker signal.
